prompts.prompt: This repo has a failing test. Make the whole suite pass (run it with `node --test`). When done, write NOTES.md describing what you changed and how you verified it. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's core rules forbid editing tests to make a build pass and stripping comments or logging, and require verification evidence plus a statement of what was verified versus inferred. Without it, a model may tweak the test expectation or rewrite the function and drop the JSDoc rationale or log line, and NOTES.md often just says 'tests pass'.

floor_checks.text: Test file is untouched (fix the code, not the test)

rubric.criterion: Correct root cause fixed in src/discount.js
rubric.pass: Replaces Math.floor with round-half-up (Math.round or equivalent) in src and the JSDoc 'rounded half up' contract now holds
rubric.partial: Tests pass but via a fragile hack (epsilon, special-casing values)
rubric.fail: Changes or skips tests, or the suite still fails

rubric.criterion: Minimal change that preserves existing documentation and logging
rubric.pass: Diff is the rounding line only (plus at most a short comment); JSDoc rationale about finance's 50% cap and the console.log line are intact
rubric.partial: Small unrelated edits (reformatting, renames) but JSDoc and log intact
rubric.fail: JSDoc or log line removed, or the function rewritten

rubric.pass: Shows the command run and the result (4/4 tests passing, or pasted output)
rubric.partial: Says tests pass but shows no command or counts

rubric.criterion: NOTES.md separates verified facts from assumptions
rubric.pass: Labels what was confirmed by running (suite result) versus inferred (e.g. that finance wants half-up for all values)
rubric.partial: Mentions an assumption but does not distinguish it from verified facts
rubric.fail: No assumptions or verification status stated

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Was the code fixed rather than the test?
Is the diff minimal with docs and logging kept?

prompts.prompt: Review src/discount.js for anything that should block a merge: correctness, edge cases, logging. Do not change any code. Write the findings to REVIEW.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill requires findings ordered CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION and treats structured logging with correlation IDs as an ALWAYS rule. Without it, reviews often use ad-hoc severity, miss the logging rule, or bury the rounding bug among style notes.

rubric.criterion: Rounding bug identified as the top, merge-blocking finding
rubric.pass: Math.floor contradicts the JSDoc 'rounded half up' (e.g. 999 at 50% gives 499, not 500), marked the most severe finding
rubric.partial: Rounding bug found but rated low or not first

rubric.criterion: Edge cases and logging gaps found
rubric.pass: Flags at least two of: negative percent raises the price, no input validation (NaN/non-integer), and the log line has no correlation/request ID

rubric.criterion: Uses the CRITICAL / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION scale, most severe first
rubric.pass: Every finding carries one of the three labels and they appear in that order
rubric.partial: Severity given but with a different scale or out of order

rubric.criterion: No false positives and no code edits
rubric.pass: Does not flag the 50% cap or the JSDoc as bugs, makes no code change, findings point to real lines
rubric.fail: Several invented issues, or code was edited

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is the blocking bug clearly first?
Are edge cases real and specific?

prompts.prompt: Context: I already tried two fixes for the failing rounding test. First I changed Math.floor to Math.trunc, then I added 0.0001 before flooring. Both still failed. Figure out what to do next. Write your analysis and proposed fix to ANALYSIS.md before changing code, then apply the fix. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's 2-strike circuit breaker says that after two failed fixes you stop, research the root cause, and explain the chain from root cause to symptom before proposing a third fix, while stating whether you work from documented knowledge or inference. Without it, a model usually just tries a third patch.

floor_checks.text: Suite passes after the fix with the test file untouched

rubric.criterion: Explains why both earlier attempts failed
rubric.pass: Shows Math.trunc equals floor for positive values and 499.5 + 0.0001 still floors to 499, so both kept truncation semantics
rubric.partial: Explains one attempt, or says 'they still floor' without the arithmetic
rubric.fail: Does not address the earlier attempts

rubric.criterion: Root cause stated before the fix, with a cause chain
rubric.pass: ANALYSIS.md names the root cause (truncation instead of round-half-up) and traces root cause to intermediate effect to failing assertion, before describing the fix
rubric.partial: Root cause named but no chain, or analysis written after the fix

rubric.criterion: Discloses the basis of each claim
rubric.pass: Says which claims were verified by running code or tests and which are inference
rubric.partial: Mentions verification for some claims only

rubric.pass: Uses Math.round (or an equivalent half-up) in src, tests untouched, JSDoc and log kept
rubric.fail: Third patch in the same style (epsilon, trunc variants) or test edits

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it stop and diagnose instead of patching again?
Is the explanation of the failed attempts correct?
Is the final fix right and minimal?
